name: WHO issues first child obesity guidelines
headline: WHO publishes its first global guidelines on child and adolescent obesity
summary: On 7 October 2026 the WHO issued its first global guidelines on obesity in children and adolescents, with one document for each age group.
keyPoints: The WHO published its first global guidelines on child and adolescent obesity on 7 October 2026.
One guideline covers children aged 29 days to under 10 years and another covers adolescents aged 10 to 19 years.
The WHO strongly recommends structured changes to diet, behaviour and physical activity for children and adolescents with obesity.

The WHO says the foundation of obesity care for children and adolescents is access to comprehensive support for healthy eating, physical activity and sustainable behaviour change, not medicines or surgery.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
The World Health Organization (WHO) issued its first global guidelines on child and adolescent obesity on 7 October 2026. The WHO describes them as evidence-informed recommendations for managing obesity in children and adolescents.

There are two documents: one for children aged 29 days to under 10 years and one for adolescents aged 10 to 19 years. The recommendations cover diet, physical activity, sedentary behaviour and sleep, behaviour-change and digital health interventions, medicines, bariatric surgery, weight-management devices and combined approaches. The WHO strongly recommends structured changes to diet, behaviour and physical activity for children and adolescents with obesity.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: The WHO says medicines, surgery and devices are not the foundation of care for children and adolescents with obesity; comprehensive support for healthy eating, physical activity and behaviour change is. It presents the guidelines as part of a life-course approach that sits alongside its existing recommendations for adults.
